title: Certificate and Public-Key Pinning Decisions Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies certificate and public-key pinning decisions?
options: Pin only for a named threat and operable endpoint, with independent backup material, monitoring, rotation, and old-client recovery.
Fetch replacement pins only after pin failure
questions.answer: Pin only for a named threat and operable endpoint, with independent backup material, monitoring, rotation, and old-client recovery.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Certificate pinning is always recommended for every Android HTTPS connection.
questions.explanation: Shipping only the current leaf pin can turn routine certificate renewal into a permanent outage for every older installed version.

questions.prompt: Why must a pin set include backup key material?
questions.answer: So a planned or emergency certificate/key change can remain trusted by already-installed app versions.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
